sections.description: Arium Comfort I product information: dual water grade output, iJust software, and TOC performance.

body.text: Arium Comfort I produces both ASTM Type 1 ultrapure water and Type 3 pure water from a single system, connected directly to a potable feed water source.
Type 1 water dispenses at rates up to 2 L/min, with quality that exceeds ASTM Type 1 specifications, not just meets them.
Type 3 pure water production runs at either 8 or 16 L/h, depending on the RO module configuration selected.
The system uses the latest reverse osmosis technology alongside a unique ion-exchange cartridge, consistently delivering purified water of the highest reproducible quality.
Intelligent iJust software makes the best use of water resources: enhancing purified water quality, reducing overall water usage, and calculating optimal cleaning cycles automatically.
Purified water is stored in the unique, closed Arium Bagtank system, reliably protecting it from secondary contamination and ensuring consistently reproducible results.

A 185/254 nm UV lamp, available as an option, prevents microbiological growth and minimizes TOC, bringing levels under 2 ppb; an optional TOC monitor checks and displays readings continuously in real time.
A touch-function display with clearly structured menu navigation ensures error-free control with a light touch, even while wearing lab gloves.
Installation adapts to available lab space: benchtop, wall-mounted, or built-in configurations are all supported.

body: Most labs need both ultrapure water for sensitive analytical work and pure water for routine tasks like glassware rinsing or feeding an autoclave. Running two separate systems for that means double the footprint, double the maintenance, and double the feed connections.
Arium Comfort I collapses that into one system, connected directly to a potable feed water source and producing both grades from the same unit.

Type 1 water reaches up to 2 L/min at a quality that exceeds ASTM Type 1 specifications, while Type 3 output runs at 8 or 16 L/h depending on whether the system is configured with one or two RO modules.
That Type 3 output also serves a quiet but valuable secondary role: purifying the feed water used to supply other ultrapure water systems downstream, extending their operational life.

It enhances purified water quality actively, rather than holding it at a static baseline, while simultaneously reducing overall water usage across daily operation.
Optimal cleaning cycles get calculated automatically by the software itself, removing the guesswork, and the risk of over- or under-cleaning, from routine maintenance.
The combined effect extends beyond convenience: guaranteed longer life for downstream ultrapure water systems that rely on Comfort I's output as feed water.

faqs.question: What is Arium Comfort II used for?
faqs.answer: It's a combined lab water system producing ASTM Type 1 ultrapure and Type 2 pure water from a potable feed, used for HPLC, AAS, ion chromatography, photometry, ELISA and RIA, media and buffer preparation, histology, and feeding laboratory instruments.

faqs.question: Does Arium Comfort II produce both Type 1 and Type 2 water?
faqs.answer: Yes. Both grades come from the same system and the same potable feed connection — Type 1 dispenses at 2 L/min, Type 2 is produced at 5 or 10 L/h depending on configuration.

faqs.question: What purification technologies does it use?
faqs.answer: Advanced reverse osmosis membranes, Sartorius's patented electrodeionization (EDI), and a cartridge with highly efficient ion-exchange resin, working in sequence.

faqs.question: What TOC level does the system achieve?
faqs.answer: Below 2 ppb in arium® water, with the 185 | 254 nm UV lamp minimizing total organic compounds as part of the purification process.

faqs.question: What does the UV lamp do?
faqs.answer: The integrated 185 | 254 nm lamp prevents microbiological growth and reduces total organic carbon in the purified water at the same time.

faqs.question: Can TOC be monitored continuously?
faqs.answer: Yes, with the optional integrated TOC monitor developed specifically for this system, which displays readings in real time.

faqs.question: What is iJust?
faqs.answer: It's the system's intelligent software — it enhances purified water quality, reduces water usage compared with conventional systems, and calculates optimal cleaning cycles rather than running them on a fixed schedule.

faqs.question: How is purified water stored?
faqs.answer: In the closed arium® bagtank system, which protects the water from secondary contamination after production.

faqs.question: Can the display be operated while wearing gloves?
faqs.answer: Yes. The touch-active display responds to a light touch through gloves, with structured menu navigation for error-free control.

faqs.question: How can the system be installed?
faqs.answer: Three ways — as a benchtop unit, wall-mounted, or built-in — so it fits the space the lab actually has available.

faqs.question: Does it extend the life of downstream instruments?
faqs.answer: Yes. Feeding autoclaves, glassware dishwashers, humidifiers, water baths, and downstream ultrapure systems with purified water lengthens their working life.

longForm.heroHook: Type 1 and Type 2 water from one system, straight off the tap feed.
longForm.heroLead: Most labs end up running two water systems: one producing Type 2 for autoclaves, dishwashers and media prep, another polishing to Type 1 for HPLC and ion chromatography. Two footprints, two consumable schedules, two things to service. Arium Comfort II produces both from a single unit connected directly to potable feed water. Reverse osmosis membranes, patented electrodeionization, and a high-efficiency ion-exchange cartridge work in sequence, so ASTM Type 1 ultrapure dispenses at 2 L/min while Type 2 pure water is produced continuously at 5 or 10 L/h depending on configuration. Purified water is held in the closed arium® bagtank, which keeps it away from the airborne contamination an open reservoir invites. And iJust software runs underneath all of it, tuning water usage and calculating cleaning cycles rather than running fixed intervals regardless of what the system actually needs.

body.text: Arium Comfort II connects directly to a potable feed water source and produces ASTM Type 1 ultrapure and Type 2 pure water from that single connection.
Three technologies work in sequence: advanced reverse osmosis membranes, Sartorius's patented electrodeionization (EDI), and a cartridge with highly efficient ion-exchange resin.
Type 1 water dispenses at 2 L/min; Type 2 production runs at 5 L/h or 10 L/h depending on the configuration selected.
The optional integrated 185 | 254 nm UV lamp does two jobs at once — suppressing microbiological growth and reducing total organic carbon, bringing TOC below 2 ppb.
An optional TOC monitor, developed specifically for this system, displays readings continuously in real time rather than requiring a separate offline check.
Purified water is stored in the closed arium® bagtank system, which protects it from secondary contamination between production and use.
iJust software enhances purified water quality, reduces overall water consumption, and calculates optimal cleaning cycles rather than running them on a fixed schedule.
The touch-active display responds through gloves, so navigating the menu doesn't mean breaking sterile technique or stopping to de-glove.
Installation works three ways — benchtop, wall-mounted, or built-in — so the system fits the bench space that exists rather than requiring a bench to be cleared for it.
Feeding downstream instruments and ultrapure systems with Type 2 water extends their service life by keeping feed water quality consistent.

body: Reverse osmosis handles the bulk removal first, taking dissolved salts, organics, and particulates out of the potable feed before anything downstream has to deal with them.
Patented electrodeionization then polishes continuously without regeneration chemicals, holding purity steady rather than degrading between service intervals the way a resin-only system does.
The ion-exchange cartridge with highly efficient resin provides the final polish that takes water to ASTM Type 1 rather than stopping at Type 2.

Because the stages run in sequence rather than as separate machines, Type 2 water is available at 5 or 10 L/h for bulk work while Type 1 dispenses at 2 L/min for analytical work — from the same unit, on the same feed line.
Adding the 185 | 254 nm UV lamp puts organic reduction and microbial control into the same step: 185 nm breaks organics down to bring TOC below 2 ppb, 254 nm suppresses microbiological growth.
Feeding autoclaves, glassware washers, and downstream ultrapure systems with this Type 2 water extends their working life, since scale and fouling are what usually shorten it.

items: A purification system that runs fixed cleaning cycles rejects water on a schedule, whether or not the membrane condition actually calls for it. That reject water is a real, recurring operating cost.
iJust calculates optimal cleaning cycles from actual system condition instead, so cleaning happens when it's needed rather than when a timer says so.
The same software reduces overall water usage compared with conventional systems, which matters most where feed water is metered, restricted, or expensive.
Product water quality improves alongside that economy — iJust enhances purified water quality rather than trading purity for consumption savings.
Downstream ultrapure systems fed by this water are guaranteed longer life, because consistent feed quality is what determines how hard their own consumables have to work.
The closed bagtank protects that carefully produced water after the fact, so quality achieved at production isn't lost to airborne contamination in storage.

heroParagraphs: Most labs end up running two water systems: one producing Type 2 for autoclaves, dishwashers and media prep, another polishing to Type 1 for HPLC and ion chromatography. Two footprints, two consumable schedules, two things to service.

Arium Comfort II produces both from a single unit connected directly to potable feed water. Reverse osmosis membranes, patented electrodeionization, and a high-efficiency ion-exchange cartridge work in sequence, so ASTM Type 1 ultrapure dispenses at 2 L/min while Type 2 pure water is produced continuously at 5 or 10 L/h depending on configuration.

Purified water is held in the closed arium® bagtank, which keeps it away from the airborne contamination an open reservoir invites. And iJust software runs underneath all of it, tuning water usage and calculating cleaning cycles rather than running fixed intervals regardless of what the system actually needs.
